title: v1-chat: harmonize output framing, stop backoff, and tool metadata propagation
author: Sofia Ramirez
release_notes: Stabilizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: introduces framing negotiation, improves stop-sequence backoff to reduce premature stream termination, and ensures tool_call metadata survives fallbacks and model switches.
description:
Motivation: Client integrations expect /v1/chat.completions parity for streaming envelopes, stop semantics, and tool/function-calling metadata. We observed two classes of mismatches in production: (1) clients that prefer framed JSON chunks lost continuity when the runtime emitted line-delimited fragments; (2) stop sequences could trigger early termination during KV-cache fragmentation or backpressure, especially with short stop tokens and interleaved tool calls. Additionally, tool_call metadata was not consistently propagated across internal fallback paths, leading to broken tool orchestration in multi-model fallbacks.

This PR implements a small negotiation layer and runtime safeguards to achieve parity while maintaining our internal streaming optimizations. Changes are backward compatible (negotiation defaults to current behavior) and covered by unit/integration tests and a compatibility test targeting popular OpenAI client behaviors.

What I changed (summary): 1) Add a lightweight framing_mode negotiation header so clients can opt-in to "framed-json" envelopes or remain on "ldjson"/line-delimited streams; server selects the most restrictive framing supported by both sides to preserve compatibility. 2) Implement a stop-sequence backoff heuristic: when short stop tokens are detected within the last N tokens and a flush would otherwise close the stream, the runtime waits up to a small jittered window to confirm termination (reduces false-positive stops under KV/cache fragmentation and bursty batching). 3) Ensure tool_call metadata (origin, tool_id, correlation_id) is serialized into the stream envelope and preserved through fallback/model-swap paths; this required changes to the coordinator and the fallback merge logic. 4) Normalized the logprobs envelope key to match OpenAI's naming for downstream tooling and added a transform for legacy clients. 5) Added docs, a compatibility test harness, and JS + Python SDK adapters for the framing negotiation header.

Checklist: - [x] API: framing negotiation header + default behaviors - [x] Runtime: backoff and safe-termination guard - [x] Tooling: persist tool_call metadata across fallbacks - [x] SDK: opt-in header in JS/Python compat adapters - [x] Tests: unit + integration + compatibility matrix - [x] Docs: compatibility note and migration guide

Commits (high-level): - c1b3d9f: negotiate framing_mode header and unit tests - 3a0f11e: runtime: stop backoff heuristic and jitter window - f9d2a0b: coordinator: preserve tool_call metadata during fallback - 7b4c621: adapt JS/Python compat layers to expose framing header - 2d8ea12: normalize logprobs envelope and update docs - 0a6f9e7: compatibility test harness and matrix results in CI

Files touched (high level): - api/openai_compat/v1/chat_adapter.py - runtime/stream/coordinator.go - runtime/stream/framing_policy.go - runtime/kv/cache_manager.cc - runtime/fallback/merge_policy.go - sdk/js/openai_compat.ts - sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py - docs/openai-v1-framing.md - tests/compat/test_stop_backoff.py - tests/compat/test_framing_matrix.js - examples/compat/framed-json-example.md

Review notes and discussion (abridged): - Anika Shah: "Can we keep the default unchanged for existing clients and gate the framed-json behavior behind an explicit header?" -> Response: default is unchanged; header is opt-in. - Liam O'Connor: "Backoff window looks fine but we should ensure it doesn't violate strict latency SLAs for paid tiers." -> Response: backoff is bounded and only applies when stop tokens are ambiguous; added a config knob per-customer and a runtime SLO guard that aborts backoff past a hard cap. - Priya Nair: "Tool metadata serialization looks good, but add a test for multi-tool call interleaving." -> Response: added test case in tests/compat/test_tool_interleave.py.

CI: initial run failed on a flaky test in tests/compat/test_framing_matrix.js (timeout). I re-ran the job, fixed a race in the test harness (use deterministic port allocation) and CI passed all checks.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals. Linear references updated: ENG-4621 moved to "Done".

Notes for operators: rollout is safe-by-default. To enable framed-json universally, ops can set framing_mode: framed-json at the customer routing policy; otherwise clients can request it via the X-Redwood-Framing header. Backoff defaults are conservative; manifest keys allow disabled behavior per-customer for low-latency SLAs.
